label: Ankle injury right after drawing a foul
explain: Players tended to leave right at the whistle, mostly on fouls with no free throws, rather than after shooting their own free throws as most NBA players did. The NBA check could only count fouls with free throws, so the two sizes can't be compared directly.

label: Any injury right after a steal by the player
explain: Leans the same way as in the NBA, but weaker and not proven, though the check had a good chance of proving a link as strong as the NBA's.

label: Hand, wrist, finger or arm injury after the other team attacked the rim
explain: About as strong as in the NBA, but too few college cases to prove it. Read play by play, it was the least convincing of the five.

label: Pulled muscle or Achilles injury right after a drive or fast-break finish
explain: Passed the bar, but on three players, all on fast-break layups or dunks. Take away any one and it would not pass: treat it as a lead.

label: Ankle injury right after a rebound
explain: About as strong as in the NBA, but too few college cases to prove it.
